name: Slow Cooker Beef Nihari (Pakistani Beef Stew)
ingredients_verbatim: 1/2 piece of a small star anise
2-3 whole cloves, ground into a powder
2-3 green cardamom pods, seeds ground into a powder
1/2 tsp fennel seeds, ground into a powder
1/4-1/2 tsp red chilli powder or cayenne
1 tbsp Homemade Nihari Masala, or sub 1/2 tbsp store-bought
1/3 cup canola or other neutral oil
1 lb (454 g) boneless beef shank meat, 2-inch cubed
unmapped: boneless beef shank (no board home; closest tracked braise cut is chuck-roast)
durum atta flour (specialty; generic flour is tracked)
why: Verified published nutrition 437 cal / 18g carb / 28g protein per serving - squarely inside the 400-650 cal, <=35g carb band with room to spare. Slow-cooker beef-shank braise, weigh-and-divide friendly to 14 servings, structurally low-carb (meat + fat + spiced gravy, thickened with just 35g atta, no rice/potato base). Pakistani cuisine adds South-Asian variety the catalog lacks, and it is not a duplicate (no nihari in digest or accepted-slugs; distinct from the taken barbacoa/short-rib/pot-roast/goulash braises). Genuine pricer-lane material: beef shank, nihari masala, star anise, cardamom and durum atta are real unmapped ingredients that exercise the queue.
confidence: high - nutrition read directly from the recipe card; only caveat is 437 sits in the lower third of the band, so our label-DB recompute has less headroom above the 400 floor than mid-band ideal.
